overview.oneLineTake: Equities are holding near records, but 24-year-high yields, a Fed still leaning toward hikes, and oil back above $100 mean the next shock likely comes from rates or crude, not earnings.
themes: Records gave way to rates: SPY closed at 777.22 (-0.24%) and QQQ at 757.73 (-0.25%) as long-end yields hit 24-year highs, paring losses after a strong 10-year auction (10y ~5.27%).

The Fed stays in hiking mode: minutes show all 19 officials backed September's 25bp hike and most see another 2026 hike as likely, but no appetite for a series of hikes; NY Fed one-year inflation expectations are the highest since May 2023.

Oil is the inflation channel again: crude headlines are back above $100 on Hormuz attacks, Tropical Storm Isaias is shutting in Gulf output (Shell and Chevron evacuating platforms), and reports say the Pentagon is preparing Iran strike options.

AI capex is turning to debt: SpaceX's $40B Nvidia GPU purchase is being financed with Apollo and banks, Oracle and Broadcom are also seeking chip debt deals, and Samsung's record Q3 profit guide sets up Micron and Nvidia as earnings-season tests.
Global bond stress and safety bids: France's debt crisis is pushing European yields and spreads wider and hitting European bank shares, while the dollar sits near its high of the year.
risks: Another leg higher in long-end yields (BMO flags a 6% long bond, Taleb warns vulnerable bonds can hurt the stock rally) would hit a narrow, mega-cap-led tape hardest.
A US strike on Iran, more Hormuz attacks, or storm damage to Gulf output could spike oil and diesel and feed the hawkish Fed path.
Leverage-funded AI spending and French or euro credit contagion are building tail risks if financing conditions tighten further.

nq.summary: NDX slipped off its record as long-end yields hit 24-year highs, then pared most of a 320-pt drop after a strong 10Y auction. The minutes kept another 2026 hike in play but showed no appetite for a series of hikes. Rates and oil, not earnings, set the tone today. Thesis: neutral, 4/10 (brief rated Low-Med), fade extremes in range. Invalidation: NDX close above 31,361 or below 30,800. NDX levels: resistance 31,225, 31,361 (record high), 31,500; support 31,117, 30,904 (Wed low), 30,800.
nq.primaryCatalyst: Fed's Waller at 3:30 PM BKK, then US jobless claims at 7:30 PM BKK (forecast 200K, previous 197K).
nq.primaryRisk: Hot claims or an oil spike pushing the 10Y back over 5.35%; Iran strike, Hormuz, or Gulf storm damage; 10Y above 5.40%.
nq.overnight: NQ quiet in a 31,403-31,459 band. Samsung guided a record Q3 operating profit of 107.4T won, but sales of 195T missed. Brent near $100, gold ~$4,108.
nq.macro: All 19 officials backed September's hike, and one-year inflation expectations are the highest since May 2023. With the 10Y at 5.28% and Gulf output shut in ahead of Tropical Storm Isaias, any oil spike feeds the hawkish path and hits long-duration tech first.
nq.volatility: VIX 15.1, VXN 21.0. VXN stays rich versus VIX into a hawkish Fed. Dealer gamma unavailable.
